title: ⌘K palette hit titles a record by its raw lookup id when the object's nameField is a lookup
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUg7BKfRBcTPyMxbLh

Filing gate ③: area-directed (area S2 of seat domain:server#5). This is the out-of-scope item of #34055 (os-dev report 6903090153), first named by the #33864 dev (os-dev report 6899087689, item 4, carried on #34055 by note 6899142203). It is the sibling of #34055 / PR #34172.

## Today

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts` `searchAll` → `renderTitle` returns `row[titlePointer]` as stored. If an object's `nameField` is a lookup-typed field (`lookup` / `master_detail` / `user`), the ⌘K palette and global search title each hit by the stored foreign key, not by the target record's title. The named producer is `sys_record_share`, whose `nameField` is `recipient_id`, a lookup. Any app object titled by a person or a parent record does the same; HotCRM's `crm_project_member` is the case behind #34055. The record header already follows the lookup (`$expand`), and since PR #34172 activity rows do too.

## Why #34172 did not take it

The resolver #34172 reuses (`resolveLookupTitles`) is a plugin-audit closure, and metadata-protocol sits below plugin-audit in the graph, so it cannot import it. Adding `$expand` to the palette's `find` would change each hit's record wire shape.

## Ask

Measure on main first: a lookup-titled object in a palette search, and the hit's title. Then follow the lookup to the target's title (ADR-0079 `titleFieldOf` on the target). The read must run as the searching user, and a refused reader keeps the bare id, the same rule as `$expand` and `referenceNameVisible` (ruling 6574398310). The hit's wire shape must not change. Seam: `spec:ObjectSchema.nameField` (lookup-typed) → `protocol-record-reads.ts` `searchAll` `renderTitle`.

Prior rulings read: ADR-0079 (record title resolver); ruling 6574398310 (`referenceNameVisible`, refused reader gets `{id, name, readRefused}` only when declared).

Reader: domain:server (metadata-protocol record reads). Size S.
